answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed when its orchard of accounts coordinates to claim the same reward or violate a shared rate limit. The ledger links payouts to verified work, not headcount, so splitting one task among a velvet swarm does not multiply earnings. To attack, someone must lock capital for every raven account and risk losing it when the coordinated pattern is proven, making mass identities costly rather than free.
